newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Airlines would support price fare hike.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Airlines would support price fare hike.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) said on Wednesday it would support any move to raise air fares because of the rising price of jet fuel.
The airline, whose latest results were partly hit by rising fuel costs, said "we would support any move to adjust fares in light of rising fuel prices."
The company made the statement in response to written questions by Reuter.

The International Air Transport Association (IATA) called on Tuesday for an emergency meeting November 13 in Geneva of its 250 members, which include SIA, to consider concerted action to counter the rise in fuel costs.
The association said members saw average worldwide prices rise to 73.9 US cents per gallon in the first nine months of 1996 compared with 65.2 cents in the same year-earlier period.
Earlier this week, SIA reported an 11.4 percent drop in operating pre-tax profits to Singapore $468 million for the six months ended September 30.
The company said the fall in profits was the result of a weak yen, a weak cargo market and rising jet fuel prices.
